_meta.description: The three Squib types the user can choose. The class is a strict one-design: every builder used the same hull form and sail plan (C10), so the types differ only where the sources say they do - the cockpit (self-draining since Rondar, C9, C10) and the sails (the new Hyde B3 / Batt designs, C11, C12) - plus estimates (E) labelled as such. Each type is a hull build plus a sail package; 'calibration' holds partial calibration.json documents merged over the defaults.

_types.label: Rondar Squib (the modern standard)
_types.summary: Rondar build (2016-2024): self-draining cockpit, so water shipped over the rail runs out through the transom. Earlier-design sails. The simulator's calibrated default.

_types.label: Classic Parker or Hunter hull (the traditional fleet)
_types.summary: Hunter (1970s-1997) or Parker (1997-2010) build: same hull form, but the cockpit is not self-draining - water shipped in gusts or chop stays aboard until the crew bails it, making the boat heavier and more tender. Assumed 15 kg over the class minimum (estimate).

_types.label: New sail package (Hyde B3 / Batt designs)
_types.summary: Rondar hull with the 2024 sail designs: a flatter foot lets the jib and main sheet closer to the centreline, a wider groove upwind and a fuller main downwind (maker's claims; the size of each effect is an estimate).

classic._label: Hunter Boats (sail numbers 158-724) and Parker Sailboats (1997-2010)

aboveMinimum.note: Older GRP hulls are often heavier than new ones (absorbed water, repairs, older fittings). Not measured: weigh the boat and change this

selfDraining.note: Self-draining cockpits came with the Rondar build; earlier boats keep the water until it is bailed (a few have been fitted with the new floor moulding, the 'hybrid Squib')

soleAboveCG.note: Lower, non-draining cockpit floor (near the waterline)

standard._label: Earlier sail designs (the simulator's calibrated default)

new._label: Hyde B3 (2024) and Batt Sails' current championship design

clMax.note: Flatter base: a little less peak lift (default 1.45)

cd0.note: Flatter base and reduced luff curve: less profile drag sheeted hard (default 0.03)

stallWidthDeg.note: 'Easier to trim upwind': a wider groove before the flow separates (default 25)

cn90.note: 'Better downwind shape' from the broader seam shape: more drive with the sail square to the wind (default 1.25)

cd0.note: Designed for the rig's forestay sag: less drag when pointing (default 0.03)

sheetMinDeg.note: Jib sheets closer to the centreline (default 10)
